identity.direction: Neutral technical case-study UI focused on trust, operational clarity, readable insurance workflows and clear separation from any insurer brand identity.

responsive.mobile: From 360px, use one-column forms and stacked detail regions; convert backoffice tables to readable row cards/list treatment when columns cannot remain legible; keep all actions keyboard/touch reachable and avoid horizontal page overflow.
responsive.tablet: From 768px, preserve single-column form readability while allowing paired low-complexity fields and compact claim-list columns; timelines remain vertically readable.
responsive.desktop: From 1024px, allow constrained two-column detail/review layouts, full claims table density and persistent operator navigation while preserving logical DOM/keyboard order.

semantic_states.default: Stable interactive or display state with no pending async work.
semantic_states.loading: Keep page context visible and show a contextual skeleton/spinner; disable duplicate mutations while preserving cancellation/navigation where safe.
semantic_states.empty: Explain a true absence of records or timeline entries and provide the next valid action when one exists.
semantic_states.filtered_empty: State that records exist conceptually but no result matches the active filter; offer filter reset without implying the data source is empty.
semantic_states.success: Confirm completion in text and preserve any returned tracking/reference data needed for the next approved step.
semantic_states.error: Show a recoverable, non-sensitive problem message with retry/navigation guidance when appropriate.
semantic_states.offline: Explain connectivity loss without fabricating cached business truth; only local untrusted form state may remain available.
semantic_states.forbidden: Permission-aware access denial; never reveal protected claim content.
semantic_states.validation: Associate field-level feedback programmatically and provide a summary for multi-field submission errors.
semantic_states.conflict: Explain stale-state or idempotency/state conflict without pretending the mutation succeeded; require authoritative refresh/retry path.
semantic_states.rate_limit: Explain throttling and safe retry timing when available; avoid automatic rapid retries.
semantic_states.401: Authentication is missing/expired; route operator users back through the approved login lifecycle without leaking protected data.
semantic_states.403: Authenticated but not authorized; present a text explanation and safe navigation away from protected content.
semantic_states.404: Resource or public tracking proof is not available; public tracking must preserve the safe collapsed-not-found behavior.
semantic_states.409: Authoritative conflict state for stale transition/idempotency scenarios; preserve user context and require explicit recovery.
semantic_states.422: Server validation/eligibility rejection; preserve entered data where safe and map errors to relevant controls.
semantic_states.429: Rate-limited state with restrained retry behavior and no request storm.

accessibility.error_association: Field errors use programmatic association; submission-level summaries link/focus affected controls where useful.
accessibility.live_regions: Async verification, submission, tracking, authentication and transition outcomes use restrained polite/assertive live announcements according to urgency.
accessibility.tables: Claims data uses semantic table markup on layouts where a table is shown; mobile transformations preserve labels and relationships.
accessibility.reduced_motion: Motion is optional, brief and non-essential; respect prefers-reduced-motion.
accessibility.focus_order: Visual rearrangement must not create a DOM/keyboard order different from the logical task sequence.
